newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe government withdraws contaminated drug.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe government withdraws contaminated drug.

text.p: Zimbabwe's government has withdrawn over 14 million antibiotic tablets from the local market after tests showed they were contaminated, Health Minister Timothy Stamps said.

In an interview with the independent Financial Gazette newspaper published on Thursday, Stamps and Tobias Dzangare, chief executive of the Zimbabwe manufacturing company Varichem Laboratories, said 40 batches of Cotrimoxazole totalling about 14.4 million tablets were contaminated on the production line.

"The case came to me and they have been ordered to withdraw the drug and, if they do it repeatedly, we will withdraw the licence," Stamps said. "But having said that, Varichem has been a responsible company and I hope it was a genuine error."
Dzangare said the contamination was discovered only last month after an eight-month production run.

Preliminary tests by the Zimbabwe Drugs Control Council showed the tablets had a fungal infection and some had also developed moulds. Zimbabwe medical authorities are investigating whether any patients suffered ill effects after taking the tablets.
